picks.headline: This $3,555 Humanoid Robot Learns New Chores in 30 Minutes, Startup Says
picks.excerpt: Flourish says it's ready to ship the first 50 units starting in December.
picks.rationale: New consumer home humanoid with price, ship date and a 30-minute chore-learning claim; fresh launch, distinct from the 09-26 Tesla Optimus production card.

picks.headline: Ever wanted a video doorbell you can use in VR? Me neither, but Anker Eufy is launch the world's first model anyway, with an eye-watering price tag (but no subscription)
picks.excerpt: With 180-degree viewing field, AI tracking, and subject framing, there's nothing the Eufy S4 video doorbell can't do.
picks.rationale: Product launch: Eufy S4 doorbell with on-device AI tracking/framing and no subscription, a counterpoint to the subscription-gated camera AI compared in the 09-27 Verge card (different product, new news).

picks.headline: Gemini and Find Hub can help you locate your important documents — here's how
picks.excerpt: You can use Find Hub and Gemini to keep track of your documents without the need for a compatible tag.
picks.rationale: Highly actionable how-to pairing Gemini with Find Hub for tagless tracking; readers can use it tomorrow, no prior Find Hub coverage.

picks.headline: Review: Apple's hyper-pricey M5 Ultra Mac Studio made me into a vibe coder
picks.excerpt: Usable local AI is a lot of fun, but how much would you pay for it?
picks.rationale: Credible hands-on of M5 Ultra as a local-AI workstation; the Apple-side answer to recent Gorgon Halo/GB300 cards, not previously covered.

picks.headline: How do translation earbuds actually work?
picks.excerpt: Translation earbuds claim high accuracy, but in real-world use, you should lower your expectations. The technology is far from mature.
picks.rationale: Explainer on the AI translation pipeline in hearables with a reality check on accuracy; rounds out the set with a wearables/audio angle.
